nonLabourLines.description: Cloud infrastructure (staging + prod) setup and first 3 months
Stripe integration testing / sandbox transaction fees
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling / consultancy

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project; estimate is based on backlog point sizing and team velocity assumptions only.
Story points map roughly to effort at ~6-7 hours per point blended across roles, adjusted by task type (integration/migration tasks weighted higher due to risk).

Backend Developer capacity is 1.5 FTE (~240 hrs/month); allocated 950 hours implies roughly 4 months of near-full utilisation across the backlog's backend-heavy items (RBAC, payments, migration, 2FA, rate limiting) - this role is the tightest constraint and may need contracting help or schedule extension.
Frontend Developer is 1.0 FTE (~160 hrs/month); 650 hours implies ~4 months of full-time work across design system, dashboard, invoice UI, accessibility, responsive layout.
QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE (~96 hrs/month) allocated 380 hours (~4 months) covering regression and feature testing, weighted toward payments, migration, RBAC and accessibility.

DevOps Engineer at 0.4 FTE (~64 hrs/month) allocated 180 hours for CI/CD setup, observability, and legacy decommission support; this is a thin allocation and pipeline/infra work should be front-loaded early in the project.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) assumed to require external consultancy/tooling spend in addition to engineering hours due to its scale (400k records, 2M invoice lines).
Accessibility pass assumed to include a paid third-party WCAG audit in addition to engineering remediation hours.
Contingency included for design system component licensing and monitoring/observability tooling.

Scenario spread (Optimistic -10%, Pessimistic +20%) reflects normal estimation uncertainty for a backlog of this size with no actuals to calibrate against; migration and payment integration are the biggest sources of variance.
All 24 backlog items are assumed in scope for this estimate; priority breakdown apportions the total line-item cost across each item's priority tier.
input.reasoning: Effort was sized from backlog story points (total 189 points) using a blended rate of ~6-7 hours/point, then split across the four staffed roles according to each task's nature (e.g., payment integration and migration are backend+devops heavy, design system and accessibility are frontend heavy, all features carry QA hours). Role hours were checked against each role's FTE capacity: Backend Developer (1.5 FTE) and Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE) are the binding constraints, each requiring roughly 4 months of near-full utilisation to absorb the backlog, while QA (0.6 FTE) and DevOps (0.4 FTE) are thinly staffed relative to the number of items needing testing and infrastructure work respectively - this is flagged as a risk in the assumptions. Non-labour costs cover cloud infrastructure, Stripe sandbox costs, a third-party accessibility audit, legacy migration tooling/consultancy, and a small contingency for licensing. The Most Likely scenario equals the sum of all line items (219,613.50 USD); Optimistic and Pessimistic scenarios apply a -10%/+20% spread to reflect estimation uncertainty, weighted toward the higher end given the complexity/risk of the payment integration and data migration tasks and the lack of historical actuals to calibrate against.

reductions.description: Descope or defer Low-priority items (PW-12 Support ticket submission, PW-18 Admin back-office, PW-19 Usage analytics, PW-23 Contract tests, PW-24 Legacy decommission) to a later phase
reductions.effect: Removes roughly 39 points of Low-priority backlog work, freeing Backend/Frontend/QA hours currently allocated to those items; portal launches with core functionality only.

reductions.description: Reduce Multi-currency support (PW-14) to a single settlement currency (USD) at launch, deferring EUR/PLN support
reductions.effect: Cuts backend and QA hours tied to FX-rate handling and multi-currency settlement logic; can be added in a later release.

reductions.description: Replace third-party WCAG 2.2 AA audit with internal QA-led accessibility testing using automated tooling (axe, Lighthouse)
reductions.effect: Removes the external audit non-labour cost; relies on existing QA Engineer hours plus automated scanning instead.

reductions.description: Phase the legacy data migration (PW-8) to migrate active accounts first and archive/cold-migrate the remainder post-launch
reductions.effect: Reduces initial migration tooling/consultancy spend and Backend/DevOps hours by narrowing first-pass scope; remaining records migrated in a follow-up project phase.
